# devbox-kvm

> A Linux x86-64 KVM virtual-machine runtime and authenticated HTTPS/RDP desktop gateway, written in Go.

## Project

- Module: github.com/define42/DevBox-Gateway-kvm; executable: devbox-kvm.
- Application entry points are at the repository root. The commands are serve,
  boot, probe, seed, and auth-user; use each command's -help for current flags.
- Default build: make devbox-kvm, or CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o devbox-kvm .
  Application builds are static with cgo disabled and use the bundled Go H.264 codec.
- make docker and its make docker-purego alias use Go H.264 with 2D rendering.
  Host GPU acceleration and native guest 3D processing are not supported.
- H264_ENCODER defaults to software. auto is a compatibility alias for software;
  nvenc is unsupported. Both office and smooth profiles cap H.264 at 30 FPS.
- Requires Go 1.26.0 or newer. Running guests requires Linux KVM access.
- This is experimental software, not a production security boundary.

## Runtime boundaries

- Managed desktops boot UEFI disks in separate worker processes. Each worker uses
  private writable disk and firmware-variable files, plus a read-only cloud-init
  seed. The gateway
  authenticates connections and proxies RDP to a private worker Unix socket.
- Starting managed desktops requires a delegated cgroup v2 memory hierarchy via
  VM_CGROUP_ROOT. KVM access alone is not sufficient.
- RDP captures the VM console; it does not create a guest XRDP session. Managed
  desktops enable stereo playback through virtio-sound and RDP; guest drivers and
  client audio redirection are required. Microphone capture is not supported.
- Managed UEFI input uses a PS/2 keyboard and virtio-input absolute tablet, with
  firmware pointer fallback. The guest needs the tablet driver for absolute
  pointer input.
- Local boot supports UEFI disks and direct Linux/PVH kernel loading. Standalone
  RDP listeners, VNC/PNG display backends, and ISO/UKI boot are not supported.
- Administrator image imports normalize standalone QCOW2 v2/v3 images in Go,
  including DEFLATE/Zstd compression, without external conversion tools. The
  writable VM backend still requires normalized standalone QCOW2 disks.
- Packages under internal/ are application implementation details. Public Go
  packages include kvm, pkg/h264, and pkg/h264/api.

## Verification and safety

Run focused tests before the full make test target; the full suite requires KVM,
network namespaces, and host tools. make test includes lint, QCOW2/UEFI, and audio
checks and an 80% repository-wide statement coverage gate. make coverage runs the
default suite with cross-package instrumentation, retaining all module packages
in the denominator. Application builds and ordinary tests disable cgo; race
tests enable it for Go's instrumentation. Use the development guide for exact
commands and optional integration checks.

Do not use live gateway disks as fixtures or publish private state, credentials,
tokens, or keys. Dated performance reviews and benchmark artifacts describe their
recorded revision, not necessarily current defaults or supported features.
